_comment: The refusal register for the research prerequisite grammar (RESEARCH_SYSTEM.md section 5, AD-M37). It is an interface between two implementations, the pipeline's reference parser (tools/research_grammar.py) and the game's C# reader, and both test that the codes they emit are exactly these. G1xx are SYNTAX refusals: the expression cannot be read. G2xx are RESOLUTION refusals: it reads, but a token names something the registries and rosters do not declare (validator rule R1). Neither side renumbers a code; a new rule takes the next free number in its family, and codes are never reused. Every code has at least one hostile case in tests/fixtures/research_grammar/cases.json.

contexts.gate: Prerequisites and Cost reducers on Technologies, Doctrines and Designs. A bare token is a technology or doctrine id.
contexts.acquisition: The Design bureau column. A bare token is a bureau of the design's own nation; comma = joint design, pipe = competing bids.
contexts.list: A plain comma list of names (Producers). No operators, no prefixes.

codes.summary: The cell holds only whitespace. An EMPTY cell means no prerequisite; a blank one is an editing accident, not a statement.
The cell contains a tab, newline or other control character (an in-cell line break, for example).
A comma with nothing on one side of it: a leading or trailing comma, or two in a row.
A pipe with nothing on one side of it.
A parenthesis is closed without being opened, or left open. Parentheses protect commas and pipes inside a name, so an unbalanced one changes how the whole cell splits.
A token has a <word>: prefix that is not in the grammar's vocabulary (prefixes are lower case and closed).
A known prefix used in a context that does not allow it: import:/seized:/captured: in a gate, flag:/design:/... in a Design bureau cell, any prefix in a plain list.
A prefix with nothing after the colon.
Whitespace directly after a prefix's colon. Names are matched exactly, so `design: Lancer Mk II` would never resolve.
A bare id contains whitespace, a parenthesis or a colon. Ids are opaque, so nothing else about their spelling is checked.
An xp: token that is not exactly xp:<branch>:<positive integer>.
A pipe in a plain list, where there are no alternatives.
A bare id that is neither a technology nor a doctrine.
A design: name that matches no design exactly.
A flag: id not declared in the registries.
A fielded: id not declared in the registries.
A focus: id not declared in the registries.
An xp: branch or tier outside the declared experience registry.
A bureau: name that is no bureau of any nation, or a bare Design bureau / Producers name that is no bureau of the design's own nation.
A licence: or import: target that is neither a bureau of any nation nor an off-map vendor.
A seized: target that is no bureau of any nation.
A captured: target that is not a nation in the data.
